items.stem: Define the term 'added value'.
items.answer: The difference between the price a business sells its product for and the cost of the bought-in materials and components used to make it.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The difference between the price a business sells its product for and the cost of the bought-in materials and components used to make it. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between added value and profit.
items.answer: Added value is selling price less the cost of bought-in materials only; profit is revenue less all costs, including wages, rent and other overheads, so profit is smaller than added value.
items.markingKey: 1 mark added value = price − bought-in materials; 1 mark profit deducts all costs; 1 mark consequence: added value must also pay labour and overheads. [3]

items.stem: Explain why the concept of opportunity cost is important when a business makes decisions.
items.answer: Resources such as finance and time are scarce, so choosing one option means giving up the next best one; comparing the benefit lost helps managers choose the option that gives the greatest return.
items.markingKey: 1 mark scarcity; 1 mark next best alternative forgone; 1 mark use in comparing options. [3]

items.stem: Tanvir Textiles is a private limited company in Dhaka, Bangladesh with about 420 staff. It makes shirts and T-shirts for European fashion retailers. Labour turnover among machinists has risen sharply this year. Explain two ways in which Tanvir Textiles could increase the added value of its shirts and T-shirts.
items.answer: Points to develop for Tanvir Textiles: added value = selling price − cost of bought-in materials; improving quality, design or service allows a higher price; building the brand increases what customers will pay; reducing waste or finding cheaper suppliers lowers input costs.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: added value = selling price − cost of bought-in materials. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Tanvir Textiles (clothing manufacturing). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. improving quality, design or service allows a higher price; building the brand increases what customers will pay. [4]

items.stem: Andes Textil SA is a family-owned private company based in Lima, Peru. It makes premium alpaca knitwear for fashion retailers in North America and Japan and employs about 320 people. The founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production. Explain how Andes Textil uses the factors of production to create its alpaca knitwear.
items.answer: Points to develop for Andes Textil: the four factors are land, labour, capital and enterprise; labour and capital transform inputs into outputs; enterprise organises the other factors and takes the risk; the transformation process adds value.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: the four factors are land, labour, capital and enterprise. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Andes Textil (textile manufacturing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. labour and capital transform inputs into outputs; enterprise organises the other factors and takes the risk. [3]

items.stem: Andina Solar SpA is a private limited company based in Santiago, Chile. It designs and installs solar power systems for farms, mines and homes and employs about 380 people. The government has announced new subsidies for business investment in renewable energy. Evaluate the most effective way for Andina Solar to increase the added value of its solar installations.
items.answer: For: branding and quality allow a premium price; efficiency lowers bought-in costs; better customer service differentiates the business. Against: price rises may reduce demand; cost cutting can harm quality; improvements take time and investment. Judgement: for Andina Solar it depends mainly on how price sensitive its customers are, and also on the strength of competitors.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Andina Solar: renewable energy, about 380 employees, private limited company in Chile; the government has announced new subsidies for business investment in renewable energy). AO3 Analysis [3]: arguments for, e.g. branding and quality allow a premium price; efficiency lowers bought-in costs; better customer service differentiates the business; arguments against, e.g. price rises may reduce demand; cost cutting can harm quality; improvements take time and investment. AO4 Evaluation [3]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on how price sensitive its customers are; the strength of competitors; the finance available. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Andina Solar. [10]

items.stem: Based in Lagos, Lagos Bites Ltd (private limited company) produces packaged snacks such as plantain chips and chin chin. The business has around 700 employees. Rising costs of imported packaging have cut its profit margins. Explain one disadvantage to Lagos Bites of raising added value through premium branding of its packaged snacks.
items.answer: Branding and promotion are expensive; this would be a problem for Lagos Bites, which produces packaged snacks such as plantain chips and chin chin.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. branding and promotion are expensive; higher prices may reduce sales volume; customers may not value the brand enough. 1 mark: explained in the context of Lagos Bites (food processing). [2]

items.stem: Explain two ways a business could increase the value it adds to its products.
items.answer: It could build a brand or improve design and quality so customers pay a higher price; or it could reduce the cost of bought-in materials by finding cheaper suppliers or reducing waste.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark method, 1 mark explanation): higher price through branding/quality/convenience/service; lower bought-in costs. [4]

Bosphorus Home sells its main product for $215 per unit. The cost of bought-in materials and components is $105 per unit. It sells 6,500 units a year. Calculate the added value per unit.

items.stem: Define the term 'entrepreneur'.
items.answer: A person who has a business idea, organises the factors of production to start a business and takes the risk of doing so.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – A person who has a business idea, organises the factors of production to start a business and takes the risk of doing so. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain two characteristics of a successful entrepreneur.
items.answer: Innovation and creativity, so they can spot opportunities and develop new ideas; and willingness to take calculated risks, because starting a business means investing time and money with no guarantee of success.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark characteristic, 1 mark explanation): e.g. innovation, risk-taking, determination/resilience, self-confidence, hard work, leadership. [4]

items.stem: Explain why intrapreneurship can benefit a large company.
items.answer: Employees who are encouraged to develop ideas create new products and processes, which keeps the company innovative, helps it respond to change and motivates and retains talented staff.
items.markingKey: 1 mark innovation; 1 mark responsiveness/competitiveness; 1 mark motivation/retention. [3]

items.stem: Clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence. IslaConnect Inc., a private limited company in the Philippines with about 2,600 employees, runs customer-service call centres for banks and airlines in the USA and Australia. Explain how IslaConnect could benefit from encouraging intrapreneurship.
items.answer: Points to develop for IslaConnect: intrapreneurs innovate inside an existing business; new products such as AI chatbot services could be developed; motivated staff are more productive and less likely to leave; faster response to competitors and changing tastes.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: intrapreneurs innovate inside an existing business. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to IslaConnect (business process outsourcing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. new products such as AI chatbot services could be developed; motivated staff are more productive and less likely to leave. [3]

items.stem: Kaya Cycles is a partnership in Mombasa, Kenya with about 9 staff. It sells and repairs bicycles and motorbikes. The two partners disagree about whether to borrow money to expand. Explain how Kaya Cycles could benefit from encouraging intrapreneurship.
items.answer: Points to develop for Kaya Cycles: intrapreneurs innovate inside an existing business; new products such as electric bicycles could be developed; motivated staff are more productive and less likely to leave; faster response to competitors and changing tastes.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: intrapreneurs innovate inside an existing business. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Kaya Cycles (retail and repairs). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. new products such as electric bicycles could be developed; motivated staff are more productive and less likely to leave. [3]

items.stem: Based in Doha, Pearl Logistics WLL (private limited company) provides freight forwarding, warehousing and lorry delivery services. The business has around 1,500 employees. Large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery. Discuss whether Pearl Logistics should give employees time to work on their own ideas.
items.answer: For: innovation could lead to new products; staff motivation and retention improve; competitive advantage over rivals. Against: cost of time away from core work; many ideas fail; difficult to manage and measure. Judgement: for Pearl Logistics it depends mainly on the culture of the business, and also on the pace of change in logistics.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Pearl Logistics: logistics, about 1,500 employees, private limited company in Qatar; large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery). AO3 Analysis [3]: arguments for, e.g. innovation could lead to new products; staff motivation and retention improve; competitive advantage over rivals; arguments against, e.g. cost of time away from core work; many ideas fail; difficult to manage and measure. AO4 Evaluation [3]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the culture of the business; the pace of change in logistics; how ideas are selected and funded. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Pearl Logistics. [10]

items.stem: Green Valley Dairy is a co-operative in Pune, India with about 80 staff. It collects milk from 900 member farmers and makes yoghurt and cheese. The members are arguing about how much of the profit to reinvest. Explain one advantage to Green Valley Dairy of relying on the founder's entrepreneurial skills.
items.answer: Quick decisions and a clear vision; this would help Green Valley Dairy, which collects milk from 900 member farmers and makes yoghurt and cheese.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. quick decisions and a clear vision; strong drive to succeed; willingness to take risks on new opportunities. 1 mark: explained in the context of Green Valley Dairy (agriculture and food processing). [2]

items.stem: A new supermarket chain wants to stock its juices if it can supply larger quantities. Sunrise Juices Ltd, a private limited company in Jamaica with about 60 employees, makes fresh fruit juices sold to supermarkets and hotels. Explain two characteristics that the founder of Sunrise Juices would need to succeed.
items.answer: Points to develop for Sunrise Juices: entrepreneurs organise resources and take risks; creativity to spot opportunities such as low-sugar smoothies; resilience to survive setbacks in food and drink manufacturing; leadership and communication to manage employees.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: entrepreneurs organise resources and take risks. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Sunrise Juices (food and drink manufacturing). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. creativity to spot opportunities such as low-sugar smoothies; resilience to survive setbacks in food and drink manufacturing. [4]

items.stem: Its biggest customer, a convenience-store chain, wants deliveries twice a day. Siam Ready Meals Co. Ltd, a private limited company in Thailand with about 1,100 employees, produces chilled and frozen ready meals for supermarkets and convenience stores. Explain two characteristics that the founder of Siam Ready Meals would need to succeed.
items.answer: Points to develop for Siam Ready Meals: entrepreneurs organise resources and take risks; creativity to spot opportunities such as plant-based ready meals; resilience to survive setbacks in food manufacturing; leadership and communication to manage employees.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: entrepreneurs organise resources and take risks. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Siam Ready Meals (food manufacturing). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. creativity to spot opportunities such as plant-based ready meals; resilience to survive setbacks in food manufacturing. [4]

items.markingKey: (a) AO1 Knowledge [2]: intrapreneurs innovate inside an existing business. items.stem: Mosaic Apps Ltd is a private limited company based in Casablanca, Morocco. It develops booking apps for restaurants and hairdressers and employs about 28 people. The founders want to raise finance from venture capitalists. Evaluate whether the personal qualities of the entrepreneur are the most important factor in the success of a new business such as Mosaic Apps.
items.answer: For: vision and determination drive the business; risk-taking allows opportunities to be exploited; leadership motivates staff. Against: access to finance is essential; the market and level of competition matter; economic conditions and government support affect success. Judgement: for Mosaic Apps it depends mainly on the nature of the market, and also on how much finance is available.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Mosaic Apps: software, about 28 employees, private limited company in Morocco; the founders want to raise finance from venture capitalists). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. vision and determination drive the business; risk-taking allows opportunities to be exploited; leadership motivates staff; arguments against, e.g. access to finance is essential; the market and level of competition matter; economic conditions and government support affect success. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the nature of the market; how much finance is available; whether the owner can build a capable team. items.stem: Define the term 'business plan'.
items.answer: A written document that describes a business, its objectives and strategies, the market it is in and its financial forecasts.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – A written document that describes a business, its objectives and strategies, the market it is in and its financial forecasts. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain two benefits to an entrepreneur of preparing a business plan.
items.answer: Planning makes the entrepreneur think through the market, costs and risks before starting, reducing the chance of failure; and it can be used to persuade banks or investors to provide finance.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark benefit, 1 mark explanation): clarifies objectives/strategy, identifies risks, raises finance, a benchmark to monitor performance. [4]

items.stem: Explain why a business plan does not guarantee the success of a new business.
items.answer: The plan is based on forecasts and assumptions about demand and costs, which may be wrong, and conditions such as competition or the economy may change after it is written.
items.markingKey: 1 mark forecasts/assumptions; 1 mark external change; 1 mark plan must be put into action well. [3]

items.stem: Gold Coast Cocoa Ltd is a private limited company based in Accra, Ghana. It buys cocoa from local co-operatives and makes premium chocolate bars and employs about 450 people. World cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months. Explain the sections that Gold Coast Cocoa should include in a business plan for launching cocoa-based beauty products.
items.answer: Points to develop for Gold Coast Cocoa: a business plan sets out objectives, strategy and forecasts; market research and analysis of competitors; the marketing plan for cocoa-based beauty products; cash-flow and profit forecasts to show finance needs.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: a business plan sets out objectives, strategy and forecasts. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Gold Coast Cocoa (confectionery). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. market research and analysis of competitors; the marketing plan for cocoa-based beauty products. [3]

items.stem: Based in Nairobi, Savanna Fresh Ltd (private limited company) grows cut flowers and green beans and exports them by air to supermarkets in Europe. The business has around 850 employees. Its largest European customer has just demanded lower prices and proof of sustainable water use. Explain why a bank would want to see a business plan before lending to Savanna Fresh.
items.answer: Points to develop for Savanna Fresh: a business plan shows the business idea and forecasts; evidence that there is demand; cash-flow forecasts show whether repayments are affordable; it shows the experience and skills of the managers.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: a business plan shows the business idea and forecasts. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Savanna Fresh (horticulture). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. evidence that there is demand; cash-flow forecasts show whether repayments are affordable. [3]

items.stem: Maple Learning Inc. is a private limited company based in Toronto, Canada. It runs an online tutoring and test-preparation platform for school students and employs about 260 people. Venture capital investors expect it to become profitable within two years. Evaluate the usefulness of a business plan to Maple Learning.
items.answer: For: helps to raise finance; identifies risks in advance; provides targets to monitor performance. Against: based on forecasts that may be wrong; takes time and may become out of date; success depends on carrying the plan out. Judgement: for Maple Learning it depends mainly on how carefully the research was done, and also on how quickly the market changes.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Maple Learning: education technology, about 260 employees, private limited company in Canada; venture capital investors expect it to become profitable within two years). AO3 Analysis [3]: arguments for, e.g. helps to raise finance; identifies risks in advance; provides targets to monitor performance; arguments against, e.g. based on forecasts that may be wrong; takes time and may become out of date; success depends on carrying the plan out. AO4 Evaluation [3]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on how carefully the research was done; how quickly the market changes; whether the plan is updated. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Maple Learning. [10]

items.stem: Which is the main reason a new business prepares a business plan when applying for a bank loan?
options: To avoid paying tax
To register as a limited company
To show the bank that the business is likely to be able to repay the loan
To guarantee the business will make a profit
items.answer: To show the bank that the business is likely to be able to repay the loan
items.markingKey: To show the bank that the business is likely to be able to repay the loan. Lenders want evidence of a viable business that can repay. [1]

items.stem: Explain why a business plan should include a section on the marketing strategy.
items.answer: It shows how the business will reach its target customers through product, price, promotion and place, giving evidence that sales forecasts are realistic.
items.markingKey: 1 mark how customers are reached (marketing mix); 1 mark supports the sales forecast/persuades lenders. [2]

items.stem: The government has announced new subsidies for business investment in renewable energy. Andina Solar SpA, a private limited company in Chile with about 380 employees, designs and installs solar power systems for farms, mines and homes. Explain the sections that Andina Solar should include in a business plan for launching battery storage systems.
items.answer: Points to develop for Andina Solar: a business plan sets out objectives, strategy and forecasts; market research and analysis of competitors; the marketing plan for battery storage systems; cash-flow and profit forecasts to show finance needs.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: a business plan sets out objectives, strategy and forecasts. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Andina Solar (renewable energy). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. market research and analysis of competitors; the marketing plan for battery storage systems. [3]

items.stem: Tejo Mobility is a public limited company in Lisbon, Portugal with about 600 staff. It assembles electric scooters and e-bikes for sale across the European Union. Battery supply problems from Asia have delayed several large orders. Explain why a bank would want to see a business plan before lending to Tejo Mobility.
items.answer: Points to develop for Tejo Mobility: a business plan shows the business idea and forecasts; evidence that there is demand; cash-flow forecasts show whether repayments are affordable; it shows the experience and skills of the managers.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: a business plan shows the business idea and forecasts. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Tejo Mobility (vehicle manufacturing). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. evidence that there is demand; cash-flow forecasts show whether repayments are affordable. [4]

items.stem: Based in Pune, Green Valley Dairy Co-operative (co-operative) collects milk from 900 member farmers and makes yoghurt and cheese. The business has around 80 employees. The members are arguing about how much of the profit to reinvest. (a) Define the term 'market analysis'. (b) Analyse why a bank would want to see a business plan before lending to Green Valley Dairy.
items.answer: (a) The section of a business plan that describes the target market, customers and competitors, based on market research. (b) A business plan shows the business idea and forecasts; evidence that there is demand; cash-flow forecasts show whether repayments are affordable; it shows the experience and skills of the managers.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark: partial definition; 2 marks: full definition. [2] (b) AO1 Knowledge [2]: a business plan shows the business idea and forecasts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the case (Green Valley Dairy: agriculture and food processing, about 80 employees, co-operative in India; the members are arguing about how much of the profit to reinvest). AO3 Analysis [4]: developed chains of reasoning showing the impact on Green Valley Dairy, e.g. evidence that there is demand; cash-flow forecasts show whether repayments are affordable; it shows the experience and skills of the managers. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 developed analysis of two points in context. [8]

items.stem: Define the term 'social enterprise'.
items.answer: A business with mainly social or environmental objectives that reinvests most of its surplus in pursuing those objectives rather than paying it to owners.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – A business with mainly social or environmental objectives that reinvests most of its surplus in pursuing those objectives rather than paying it to owners. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: The "planet" element of the triple bottom line refers to
options: environmental objectives
social objectives
profit objectives
growth objectives
items.answer: environmental objectives
items.markingKey: environmental objectives. People, planet and profit: planet means environmental sustainability. [1]

items.stem: Explain the meaning of the triple bottom line.
items.answer: Social enterprises judge success on three objectives: making a surplus (profit), benefiting people such as employees and communities (social), and protecting the environment (planet).
items.markingKey: 1 mark economic; 1 mark social; 1 mark environmental. [3]

items.stem: Based in Kuala Lumpur, BatikPay Sdn Bhd (private limited company) runs a mobile payments app used by 4 million customers and 90 000 small shops. The business has around 210 employees. The central bank has announced tighter rules on data protection for payment apps. Explain how BatikPay could adopt the triple bottom line.
items.answer: Points to develop for BatikPay: the triple bottom line covers profit, people and planet; social aims such as training local workers; environmental aims such as reducing waste in producing mobile payment services; profits are still needed to fund these aims.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: the triple bottom line covers profit, people and planet. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to BatikPay (financial technology). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. social aims such as training local workers; environmental aims such as reducing waste in producing mobile payment services. [3]

items.stem: Shareholders are pressing for higher dividends while engineers want more spending on research. Lumen Robotics plc, a public limited company in Singapore with about 2,400 employees, designs and builds robots used on factory assembly lines. Evaluate whether Lumen Robotics should become a social enterprise.
items.answer: For: stronger brand with ethical consumers; more motivated staff; access to grants. Against: lower returns for owners; harder to raise finance; higher costs may make it uncompetitive. Judgement: for Lumen Robotics it depends mainly on the owners' objectives, and also on how much customers value social aims.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Lumen Robotics: industrial engineering, about 2,400 employees, public limited company in Singapore; shareholders are pressing for higher dividends while engineers want more spending on research). AO3 Analysis [2]: arguments for, e.g. stronger brand with ethical consumers; more motivated staff; access to grants; arguments against, e.g. lower returns for owners; harder to raise finance; higher costs may make it uncompetitive. AO4 Evaluation [2]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the owners' objectives; how much customers value social aims; competition in industrial engineering. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Lumen Robotics. [8]

items.stem: Explain why a social enterprise still needs to make a profit.
items.answer: It must cover its costs to survive, and the surplus is needed to reinvest in its social or environmental aims and to grow.
items.markingKey: 1 mark survival/covering costs; 1 mark surplus funds the social objective. [2]

items.stem: Andina Solar is a private limited company in Santiago, Chile with about 380 staff. It designs and installs solar power systems for farms, mines and homes. The government has announced new subsidies for business investment in renewable energy. Explain the difficulties a social enterprise in renewable energy may face.
items.answer: Points to develop for Andina Solar: social enterprises have social as well as financial objectives; higher costs from paying fair wages or using sustainable materials; harder to attract investors seeking a return; conflicts when profit and social aims clash.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: social enterprises have social as well as financial objectives. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Andina Solar (renewable energy). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. higher costs from paying fair wages or using sustainable materials; harder to attract investors seeking a return. [4]

items.stem: Which of the following is an example of capital as a factor of production?
options: A field used to grow wheat
The risk taken by a business owner
A delivery van owned by a business
The skills of a shop assistant
items.answer: A delivery van owned by a business
items.markingKey: A delivery van owned by a business. Capital means man-made resources used to produce other goods, such as machinery and vehicles. [1]

items.stem: Kiwi Trails Ltd is a private limited company based in Auckland, New Zealand. It runs guided hiking, kayaking and cycling tours and employs about 90 people. Bookings are highly seasonal and most guides are employed only for the summer. Identify and explain one advantage for Kiwi Trails of reducing the cost of bought-in materials for its adventure tours.
items.answer: Added value rises if the price stays the same; this would help Kiwi Trails, which runs guided hiking, kayaking and cycling tours.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. added value rises if the price stays the same; more competitive prices possible; higher profit margins. 1 mark: explained in the context of Kiwi Trails (tourism). [2]

items.stem: Venture capital investors expect it to become profitable within two years. Maple Learning Inc., a private limited company in Canada with about 260 employees, runs an online tutoring and test-preparation platform for school students. Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to Maple Learning of reducing the cost of bought-in materials for its online tutoring subscriptions.
items.answer: Advantage: added value rises if the price stays the same. Disadvantage: cheaper materials may reduce quality.
items.markingKey: For each point: 1 mark identification, 1 mark explanation applied to Maple Learning. Advantages: added value rises if the price stays the same; more competitive prices possible; higher profit margins. Disadvantages: cheaper materials may reduce quality; reputation may suffer; supplier relationships may be damaged. [4]

items.stem: Lotus Spa sells its main product for $300 per unit. The cost of bought-in materials and components is $176 per unit. It sells 12,500 units a year. Calculate the added value per unit.
Kiwi Trails sells its main product for $100 per unit. The cost of bought-in materials and components is $62 per unit. It sells 37,500 units a year. Calculate the added value per unit.

Kiwi Trails Ltd is a private limited company based in Auckland, New Zealand. It runs guided hiking, kayaking and cycling tours and employs about 90 people. Bookings are highly seasonal and most guides are employed only for the summer. Discuss whether increasing added value is more important than increasing sales volume for Kiwi Trails.
items.answer: For: higher added value gives a higher margin on every unit; a premium position is harder for rivals to copy; fewer units need to be sold to cover costs. Sunrise Juices sells its main product for $310 per unit. The cost of bought-in materials and components is $92 per unit. It sells 3,000 units a year. (a) Calculate the added value per unit. (b) Calculate the total added value for the year. (c) Calculate the added value as a percentage of the selling price. items.answer: (a) $218 (b) $654,000 (c) 70.3% (d) $207; lower added value leaves less to pay wages, overheads and profit. items.markingKey: (a) $310 − $92 [1]; = $218 per unit [1] [2] (b) $218 × 3,000 [1]; = $654,000 [1] [2] (c) $218 ÷ $310 × 100 [1]; = 70.3% [1] [2] (d) $321 − $114 = $207 [1]; consequence explained [1] [2] (e) AO1 Knowledge [1]: opportunity cost is the next best alternative forgone. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Sunrise Juices (food and drink manufacturing). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. finance used here cannot be used to improve existing fresh fruit juices; management time is diverted from the core business. [4]
